name: HIAD_2.2_EHSP_Cause_Machine_Readable_Codebook
scope_note: EHSP causes are root causes; an initiating cause alone is not coded as an EHSP root cause.

decision_policy.minimum_evidence: At least one explicit rule match in narrative text; generic component failure alone is insufficient.

labels.official_definition: Inadequate mechanical integrity measures; corrosion-related loss of integrity; inadequate design of pressure relief valves, venting components; lack of attention to risk of hydrogen accumulation; inappropriate material choices; unwanted hydrogen generation; inadequate process hazards analysis; inadequate operating procedures.
labels.inclusion: The narrative explicitly attributes a root cause to design, technical risk assessment, mechanical-integrity provisions, relief/venting, hydrogen accumulation control, material selection, unwanted hydrogen generation, hazard analysis, or operating-procedure design.
labels.exclusion: Do not use for a component failure without design evidence; wrong physical installation is C03; lack of maintenance or inspection is C04; individual mistake is C05; organizational safety-system failure may additionally be C06.

rules.pattern: \bcorrosion[- ]related\s+(loss|failure)|\bloss of integrity due to corrosion\b|\binappropriate material (choice|selection)\b|\bunwanted hydrogen generation\b

labels.official_definition: For example, material compatibility; failure due to ageing of (sub)-components (welds, flanges, O-rings, gaskets, seals, etc.); premature opening of the burst disks.
labels.inclusion: The narrative explicitly identifies material incompatibility/defect, manufacturing defect, ageing-related component degradation, or premature burst-disk opening as a root cause.
labels.exclusion: A leak, rupture, weld failure, membrane failure, gasket failure, or component failure alone is insufficient. Corrosion-related integrity loss is C01 under the HIAD definition unless a manufacturing/material defect is separately stated.

rules.pattern: \b(material incompatib|incompatible material|material defect|defective material|manufacturing defect|manufacturing error|fabrication defect|fabrication error)

labels.official_definition: For example, wrong consumables replacement after maintenance; components erroneously installed (one-way valves; bolts with wrong dimension, not properly sitting in the flange).
labels.inclusion: The narrative explicitly states incorrect installation, assembly, seating, connection, dimensions, orientation, or wrong replacement during maintenance.
labels.exclusion: Do not infer installation error solely because failure followed maintenance. Maintenance omission is C04; operator mistake without an installation act is C05.

labels.official_definition: Lack of (clear) instructions; lack of maintenance or inspection - poorly maintained equipment; training and enforcement of safety practice and procedures; high workload; noisy and unpleasant working conditions; constant disturbances and interruptions.
labels.inclusion: The narrative explicitly identifies inadequate instructions, maintenance, inspection, training/enforcement, workload, working conditions, disturbances, or interruptions at the job/task level.
labels.exclusion: An individual mistake is C05 unless a job-system condition is stated. Organization-wide planning, responsibility, barriers, health-and-safety management, or culture is C06 and may co-occur.

labels.official_definition: Individual/human factors, i.e. inadequate skill and competence levels; individual medical problems; mistakes, etc.
labels.inclusion: The narrative explicitly attributes the root cause to an individual error, mistake, skill/competence deficit, or medical condition.
labels.exclusion: Do not infer human factors merely because a worker operated equipment. Use C04 for deficient instructions/training/work conditions and C06 for organizational causes; multilabel is allowed when both levels are explicit.

labels.official_definition: Poor work planning; leading to high work pressure; lack of safety systems and barriers; failure to learn from previous incidents; management too biased to one-way communications; lack of co-ordination and clear definition of responsibilities; poor management of health and safety; poor safety culture.
labels.inclusion: The narrative explicitly identifies organization/management-level planning, safety systems/barriers, learning, communication, coordination, responsibility, H&S management, or safety culture deficiencies.
labels.exclusion: Task-level maintenance/instruction/training is C04 unless an organizational management cause is separately stated. Individual error is C05.

rules.evidence: safety system or organizational learning deficiency

rules.pattern: \bpoor (management of )?(health and safety|safety management|safety culture)\b|\bweak safety culture\b

labels.official_definition: Lightning, earthquake, flooding. Galvanic corrosion is not an example of force majeure; it is part of technical risk assessment and therefore does not belong to this category.
labels.inclusion: Lightning, earthquake, or flooding is explicitly identified as a causal/root-causal factor.
labels.exclusion: Galvanic corrosion and ordinary technical corrosion are not C07. Weather mentioned only as background without a causal statement is insufficient.

labels.official_definition: No definition text is present in the source row; operationally, the root cause cannot be determined from the available event information.
labels.inclusion: Use only when no C01-C07 candidate is supported and the narrative explicitly says the root cause is unknown/undetermined, or the root-cause-analysis field is empty.
labels.exclusion: C08 is mutually exclusive with C01-C07. A rule engine's failure to match a sufficiently detailed narrative does not by itself prove Unknown; classify that case as no_candidate/review_required.

rules.pattern: \b(root )?cause (is|was|remains)?\s*(unknown|undetermined|not determined|not identified|unclear)\b|\bcould not be determined\b|\bno definitive cause\b
